item.title: Does UVA XC need a national title to be considered elite?
item.dc:creator: Lucy Wooden
item.description:
Despite not winning a national championship in the past five seasons, UVA Men’s Cross Country has stood out when it comes to its competition. Much of their success has come in the past five seasons, especially when it comes to the ACC Championships and the NCAA Championships. 

Winning a national championship can often be seen as a benchmark for an elite program. Just look at Northern Arizona or Oklahoma State. Between them, the two programs have claimed four national titles in the past five seasons, including back-to-back championships. 

UVA’s program is different. While they don’t have the national championship, they have the depth and consistency. The Cavaliers have continually reloaded their top 7 and continued to have strong showings in ACC Championships, NCAA Southeast Regional Championships, and NCAA Championships. 

The question at hand is whether consistent success and competitiveness instead of a national title makes a program elite. Let’s take a look at UVA’s performances over the past five seasons. 

TFRRS XC is the official data provider for race results and team finishes across all NCAA cross country teams. Using the team and individual results from 2021 through 2025, we can look at how consistent and competitive UVA has been against some of the best teams in the country. 

One way to measure success for a program is to look at how it competes within its own conference. The ACC is by no means an easy conference to compete against. UVA has competed against teams who consistently end up at the national championships and punch automatic bids. 

Despite this level of competition, UVA has the sixth fastest 8k average across the past five seasons. UVA’s average sits right at 23:50. This translates to an average of 4:44 per mile or 2:56 per kilometer.

Code 
library(tidyverse)

acc_team_2021 <-read.csv("acc_championship_team_results21.csv") |> 
  mutate(Year=2021)

acc_team_2022 <- read.csv("acc_championship_team_results22.csv") |> 
  mutate(Year=2022)

acc_team_2023 <- read.csv ("acc_championship_team_results23.csv") |>
  mutate(Year= 2023)

acc_team_2024 <- read.csv ("acc_championship_team_results24.csv") |> 
  mutate(Year= 2024)

acc_team_2025 <- read.csv ("acc_championship_team_results25.csv") |> 
  mutate(Year= 2025)

acc_teamresults <- bind_rows (
  acc_team_2021, 
  acc_team_2022, 
  acc_team_2023, 
  acc_team_2024, 
  acc_team_2025
)

acc_decimal_times <- acc_teamresults |>
  separate(Avg..Time, into= c("minutes", "seconds", "milliseconds"), sep=":") |>
  mutate(DecimalTime= as.numeric(minutes) + (as.numeric(seconds)/60))

avg_time_2021_2025 <- acc_decimal_times |> 
  group_by(Team) |> 
  summarise(
    avg_time_2021_2025 = mean(DecimalTime)
  ) |>
  arrange(avg_time_2021_2025) 

uva <- avg_time_2021_2025 |>
  filter(
    Team == "Virginia"
  )
ggplot() + 
  geom_bar(data=avg_time_2021_2025, aes(x=reorder(Team,avg_time_2021_2025), weight=avg_time_2021_2025), fill="#232D4B") +
  geom_bar(data=uva, aes(x=reorder(Team, avg_time_2021_2025), weight=avg_time_2021_2025 ), fill="#E57200") +
  coord_flip()+
  labs(
    x="ACC Teams", 
    y="Average 8K Team Time from 2021-2025", 
    title="How does UVA's average 8K time compare in ACC Championships?", 
    subtitle="A comparison of ACC Average 8K Times from 2021-2025.", 
    caption="Source: TFRRS XC | By Lucy Wooden"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8), 
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size=10), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot"
  )

UVA ends up sitting in the top half of the ACC behind Wake Forest, North Carolina, Notre Dame, Syracuse, and Stanford. Their average 8k time from 2021 to 2025 is roughly 30 seconds behind the top team, Stanford. In a conference this deep, a margin of 30 seconds is enough to keep UVA competitive and consistent against their competition. UVA is consistent in showing up at the ACC Championships with fast times. 

Every team’s journey to the national championship begins at the regional meet. For UVA this would be the Southeast Regional meet. The top two teams receive automatic bids to the championship along with 14 at-large teams selected by a committee. If UVA men’s cross country has an elite program, their difference in how they run at the regional with how they run at the national meet will be small. A team that has a close margin between the 10k averages can handle both levels of competition. 

Code 
ncaa_team_2021 <-read.csv("ncaa_championship_team_results21.csv") |> 
  mutate(Year=2021)

ncaa_team_2022 <- read.csv("ncaa_championship_team_results22.csv") |> 
  mutate(Year=2022)

ncaa_team_2023 <- read.csv ("ncaa_championship_team_results23.csv") |>
  mutate(Year= 2023)

ncaa_team_2024<- read.csv ("ncaa_championship_team_results24.csv") |> 
  mutate(Year= 2024)

ncaa_team_2025 <- read.csv ("ncaa_championship_team_results25.csv") |> 
  mutate(Year= 2025)

ncaa_southeast_team_2021 <-read.csv("ncaa_southeast_region_team_results21.csv") |> 
  mutate(Year=2021)

ncaa_southeast_team_2022 <- read.csv("ncaa_southeast_region_team_results22.csv") |>
  mutate(Year=2022)

ncaa_southeast_team_2023 <- read.csv ("ncaa_southeast_region_team_results23.csv") |> mutate(Year= 2023)

ncaa_southeast_team_2024<- read.csv ("ncaa_southeast_region_team_results24.csv") |>
  mutate(Year= 2024)

ncaa_southeast_team_2025 <- read.csv ("ncaa_southeast_region_team_results25.csv") |>
  mutate(Year= 2025)

ncaa_team_results <- bind_rows(
  ncaa_team_2021, 
  ncaa_team_2022, 
  ncaa_team_2023, 
  ncaa_team_2024, 
  ncaa_team_2025
)

ncaa_southeast_team_results <- bind_rows(
  ncaa_southeast_team_2021, 
  ncaa_southeast_team_2022, 
  ncaa_southeast_team_2023, 
  ncaa_southeast_team_2024, 
  ncaa_southeast_team_2025
)

ncaa_southeast_team_results <- bind_rows(
  ncaa_southeast_team_2021, 
  ncaa_southeast_team_2022, 
  ncaa_southeast_team_2023, 
  ncaa_southeast_team_2024, 
  ncaa_southeast_team_2025
)

ncaa_championship_decimal_times <- ncaa_team_results |>
  separate(Avg..Time, into= c("minutes", "seconds", "milliseconds"), sep=":") |>
  mutate(DecimalTime= as.numeric(minutes) + (as.numeric(seconds)/60))

ncaa_southeast_decimal_times <- ncaa_southeast_team_results |>
  separate(Avg..Time, into= c("minutes", "seconds", "milliseconds"), sep=":") |>
  mutate(DecimalTime= as.numeric(minutes) + (as.numeric(seconds)/60))

avg_ncaa_time_2021_2025 <- ncaa_championship_decimal_times |> 
  group_by(Team) |> 
  summarise(
    avg_ncaa_time_2021_2025 = mean(DecimalTime)
  ) |>
  arrange(avg_ncaa_time_2021_2025) 

avg_southeast_time_2021_2025 <- ncaa_southeast_decimal_times |> 
  group_by(Team) |> 
  summarise(
    avg_southeast_time_2021_2025 = mean(DecimalTime)
  ) |>
  arrange(avg_southeast_time_2021_2025) 

combined_data <- inner_join(avg_ncaa_time_2021_2025, avg_southeast_time_2021_2025)

final_data <- combined_data |>
  group_by(Team) |> 
  summarise(
    ncaa_championship = sum(avg_ncaa_time_2021_2025), 
    ncaa_southeast = sum(avg_southeast_time_2021_2025))

ggplot() + 
  geom_segment(
    data=final_data, 
    aes(
      y=reorder(Team, ncaa_championship), yend=Team,
      x=ncaa_championship, xend=ncaa_southeast),
    color="grey",
    linewidth = 1.0,
  ) + 
  geom_point(
    data=final_data,
    aes(
      y=Team,
      x=ncaa_championship,
      color="NCAA Championship Average 10K Time"
    ),
    size=1.5
  ) + 
  geom_point(
    data=final_data,
    aes(
      y=Team,
      x=ncaa_southeast,
      color="NCAA Southeast Regional Average 10K Time"
    ),
    size=1.5
  )+ 
  scale_color_manual(name="Average 10K Times from 2021-2025 ", values=c("#232D4B", "#E57200"))+
  labs(
    x="NCAA Championship and NCAA Southeast Regional Average 10K Times", 
    y="Teams",  
    title="How do 10k times differ from the Southeast Regional to the NCAA Championship?", 
    subtitle="Average 10k times for the Southeast Regional and the NCAA Championship from 2021-2025.", 
    caption="Source: TFRRS XC | By Lucy Wooden"
  ) + 
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8), 
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size=10), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot"
  )

UVA’s 10k average time changed by only 4 seconds between the Southeast Regional performances and NCAA Championship performances. Additionally, the small gap between the Southeast Regional performance and the NCAA Championship showcases the runners aren’t peaking too early in their season and are staying consistent in meets. 

Cross country scores a team’s top five runners, which means the performances and times of those runners is crucial to a team’s depth. If UVA is to be considered an elite program, their top 5 runners should finish close together and should be getting faster over time.

Code 
library(gt)

acc21 <- read.csv("acc_championship_individual_results21.csv") |> 
  mutate(Year=2021)

acc22 <- read.csv("acc_championship_individual_results22.csv")|> 
  mutate(Year=2022)

acc23 <- read.csv("acc_championship_individual_results23.csv")|> 
  mutate(Year=2023) 

acc24 <- read.csv("acc_championship_individual_results24.csv")|> 
  mutate(Year=2024)

acc25 <- read.csv("acc_championship_individual_results25.csv")|> 
  mutate(Year=2025)

acc_results <- bind_rows (
  acc21, 
  acc22, 
  acc23, 
  acc24, 
  acc25
)

acc_results |> 
  separate(TIME, into= c("minutes", "seconds", "milliseconds"), sep=":") |>
  mutate(decimal_time= as.numeric(minutes) + (as.numeric(seconds)/60)) |> 
  filter(TEAM== "Virginia") |> 
  group_by(Year) |>
  top_n(5, wt=-decimal_time) |> 
  select(NAME,Year, decimal_time) |> 
  gt()|>
  data_color(
    columns = decimal_time,
    method = "numeric",
    palette = c("#232D4B", "#E57200"),
    domain = c(22, 25),
    reverse = TRUE
  )|> 
  cols_label(
    NAME = "Top 5 Runners for UVA at the ACC Championship",
    decimal_time = "8K Finish Time"
  )|>
  tab_header(
    title = "How have UVA's Top 5 finished at the ACC Championships?",
    subtitle = "The 8k finish times have only seen a small margin of difference from 2021-2025."
  )|> tab_style(
    style = cell_text(color = "black", weight = "bold", align = "left"),
    locations = cells_title("title")
  ) |> tab_style(
    style = cell_text(color = "black", align = "left"),
    locations = cells_title("subtitle")
  )|>
  tab_source_note (
    source_note = md("**By:** Lucy Wooden  |  **Source:** TFRRS XC")
  )|>
  tab_style(
    locations = cells_column_labels(columns = everything()),
    style = list(
      cell_borders(sides = "bottom", weight = px(3)),
      cell_text(weight = "bold", size=15)
    )
  ) |>
  opt_row_striping() |> 
  opt_table_lines("none") |> 
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_row_groups()
  )

The results from the past five ACC Championships demonstrate this eliteness. In 2021, UVA’s top five averaged 24:32 for 8k. In 2025, the runners averaged 23:01. This is around a 90 second difference across the top 5 runners. This is what depth and eliteness looks like in a cross country program. 

Whether or not you think a national championship defines an elite program, UVA has consistently proved that they belong in this conversation.
